subject: FY25 Community Preservation Budget and Annual Plan
overview: The committee approved a $5,000 grant for a citywide park tree inventory and established its fiscal year 2025 budget, increasing the minimum set-aside for affordable housing to 15%. Members also reviewed a draft update of the Community Preservation Plan and discussed strategies for addressing a significant decrease in state matching funds.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Accepted the meeting minutes from March 12 and April 9, 2024.

items.title: Trees Medford Small Grant Application
items.summary: Approved a $5,000 small grant for Trees Medford to inventory approximately 1,000 trees in city parks to support the city's GIS data and vulnerability assessments. The committee discussed whether to fund the request through administrative or programmatic budgets before opting for the latter to ensure public transparency via City Council review.

items.title: Annual Plan Update
items.summary: Reviewed the 2024 Community Preservation Plan draft, which highlights that 35% of completed city park projects since 2020 utilized CPA funds. Discussion focused on the projected drop in the state match to 14.5% and the strategic goal of maintaining a balance between the three program areas despite increased public pressure to prioritize housing.

items.title: FY25 Budget Disbursement
items.summary: Approved the annual budget allocation, setting set-asides at 10% for open space, 10% for historic preservation, and an increased 15% for affordable housing, with the remaining 60% held in general reserves. The higher housing allocation was adopted as a symbolic gesture to address community needs while maintaining flexibility for various project types.

items.title: Application Materials Review
items.summary: Discussed improvements to the online Smartsheet application, including embedding editable templates of successful past grants to assist applicants who cannot save progress within the form.

items.title: Membership and General Updates
items.summary: Received updates on the search for two at-large committee vacancies and noted the completion of the World War I Memorial statue restoration.
